moods.label: Calm
moods.msg: A calm moment is a good time to do something worth remembering. A few ideas:

moods.label: Good
moods.msg: Glad you are feeling good. Here are a few ways to make the most of it:

moods.label: Tired
moods.msg: Being tired is a signal, not a failure. These ask very little of you:

moods.label: Restless
moods.msg: That restless energy can go somewhere good. Try one of these:

moods.label: Anxious
moods.msg: That sounds like a lot to carry. These might help you slow down a little:

moods.label: Low
moods.msg: I am sorry today feels heavy. No pressure, but here are a few small, kind things:

moods.label: Lonely
moods.msg: Feeling lonely is hard, and more common than it looks. These might help you feel more connected:

subject: the stars you can see tonight
a historical figure you know little about
how bridges stay up
why the sky changes colour
the history of your city
a bird you often see
how your favourite food is made
the moon’s phases
area: an old part of your city
the streets around a railway station

actions.d: One continuous line, no erasing, no judging.
actions.w: Drawing makes you actually look, the opposite of scrolling.

actions.t: Make a picture using only {colour} things
actions.d: Gather {count} {colour} objects and arrange them into a little artwork.
actions.w: A playful creative puzzle with a real finish line.
s: Arrange them on a table or floor
Photograph it, then put everything back

actions.d: Eight lines, any style, rhyming optional.
actions.w: Making something beats consuming something.
s: Write the title at the top

actions.d: Doodle nothing but {shape} until the page is full.
actions.w: Repetitive drawing is surprisingly calming.
s: Keep going until the page is full

actions.d: A whole story in exactly six words. Write five versions.
actions.w: Tiny, quick and oddly absorbing.

actions.d: Something small and handmade for a person you like.
actions.w: Making for someone else doubles the good feeling.

actions.t: Walk to {place} and sit for ten minutes
actions.d: No headphones. Just sit and notice.
actions.w: Your mind gets room to wander, which is where good ideas show up.
s: Leave your phone in your pocket
Sit for ten minutes and notice three things

actions.d: A colour hunt around your neighbourhood.
actions.w: A small quest that makes ordinary streets interesting.

actions.d: Catch the light changing, at sunrise or sunset if you can.
actions.w: The best free show there is.

actions.d: Stand still for ten minutes and pay attention to {sound}.
actions.w: Trains patient attention, and it is restful.
s: Close your eyes and listen for {sound}

actions.t: Take the long way to a {newplace}
actions.d: Pick a route you have never walked.
actions.w: New routes make familiar places feel new.
s: Take a street you never use

actions.d: Thirty seconds of your real voice, saying you thought of them.
actions.w: Voice carries warmth that text cannot.
s: Think of one memory you share

actions.d: No agenda, just say hi.
actions.w: One real conversation does more than an hour of feeds.
s: Open with “I was just thinking about you”
Ask one question about their week

actions.t: Invite someone for {cuisine} food this week
actions.d: Suggest a specific day and place.
actions.w: Plans with a time attached actually happen.
s: Suggest a day and a place

actions.d: Phones in another room, best of three.
actions.w: Shared play is one of the quickest ways to feel close.

actions.d: A message or call with one good question.
actions.w: People light up when asked about what matters to them.
s: Ask: “What is a memory you still smile about?”

actions.d: Hello, thank you, and a few you like.
actions.w: Tiny, finishable learning with a real sense of progress.
s: Say each one out loud three times

actions.d: Practise until you can do it once without help.
actions.w: A new skill you can show someone tonight.

actions.t: Read about {subject}, then explain it to someone
actions.d: Twenty minutes of reading, two minutes of teaching.
actions.w: Explaining something is the best way to learn it.
s: Read one good article or chapter

actions.t: Read one chapter of a paper book
actions.d: Phone in another room, one chapter only.
actions.w: Deep attention is a muscle; this is a gentle workout.

actions.t: Drink a cup of tea doing nothing else
actions.d: Make it slowly and drink it slowly.
actions.w: Ten quiet minutes of just one thing.

actions.t: Breathe in for 4 and out for 6, {count} times
actions.d: Slow breathing, sitting or lying down.
actions.w: Long out-breaths help your body settle.

actions.t: Write {count} things you are grateful for
actions.d: Small things count, like a good meal or a kind message.
actions.w: Gratitude written down sticks better.

actions.d: Move your attention from toes to head.
actions.w: A quick reset when your head feels noisy.
s: Notice each part of your body

actions.d: Walk and name one good thing every minute.
actions.w: Movement and a mood lift together.
s: Each minute, name one good thing
Save the best one in your Journal

actions.d: Short rounds, rest between, at your own pace.
actions.w: Burns restless energy fast and leaves you clearer.

actions.d: Door closed, volume up.
actions.w: A few songs can change your whole mood.

actions.d: Fast enough to breathe a little harder.
actions.w: Restless energy gets somewhere useful to go.

actions.d: Neck, shoulders, back and hips, slowly.
actions.w: Undo the phone posture.

actions.t: Cycle to a {newplace} instead of riding
actions.d: Turn a short trip into movement.
actions.w: A chore becomes fresh air.

actions.d: A familiar dish with {ingredient} added.
actions.w: Small novelty and a result you can taste.
s: Write down how it turned out

actions.d: Pick one dish from {cuisine} cooking you have never made.
actions.w: Learning through taste is the most fun kind.

actions.d: Quick, fresh and big on flavour.
actions.w: Big flavour from a few minutes of work.
s: Have it with your next meal

actions.d: Something simple, made for another person.
actions.w: Feeding someone is one of the oldest ways to show care.

actions.t: Listen to a full {genre} album, lights off
actions.d: Start to finish, no skipping.
actions.w: Real listening is different from background noise.

actions.d: Ten songs that remind you of them.
actions.w: A gift that says “I know you”.
s: Put them in a good order
Send it with one line about why

actions.t: Learn the chorus of a {genre} song
actions.d: Sing or play it until you know it by heart.
actions.w: Making music is more absorbing than consuming it.
s: Perform it once, even to an empty room

actions.d: Full volume, every word.
actions.w: Singing releases tension and lifts your mood.
s: Sing them all the way through

actions.t: Help a neighbour with one small thing
actions.d: Carry something, water plants, or just ask.
actions.w: Belonging starts on your own street.

actions.t: Give away {count} {item} you do not use
actions.d: Someone else could use them.
actions.w: A lighter home and a useful gift.
s: Find a local donation spot or person

actions.d: A bag, gloves and twenty minutes.
actions.w: Visible good you can see straight away.

actions.t: Thank a local worker in person
actions.d: A shopkeeper, guard, cleaner or teacher.
actions.w: People rarely hear how much they matter.
s: Learn their name if you do not know it

actions.d: Empty it, wipe it, put back only what belongs.
actions.w: A visible win in minutes, and a calmer head.
s: Put back only what you use

actions.d: A loose handle, a wobbly chair, a dead bulb.
actions.w: A small repair is a big feeling of competence.
s: Find out how to fix it

actions.t: Sort your {item} into keep and give away
actions.d: Two piles, no maybes.
actions.w: Less clutter, more space to breathe.
s: Put the give-away pile by the door

actions.t: Print a photo and put it on the wall
actions.d: One photo you love, off your phone.
actions.w: Memories you see daily beat ones buried in a gallery.
s: Stick or frame it somewhere visible

actions.d: With anyone who is around.
actions.w: Strategy and laughter with someone across from you.

actions.t: Fold a paper plane and fly it {count} times
actions.d: Try to beat your own distance each time.
actions.w: Silly, joyful and impossible while scrolling.
s: Adjust the wings to go further

actions.d: Play one round with your house rule.
actions.w: Changing the rules makes an old game new.

actions.d: Find wind and open space.
actions.w: Outdoors, playful and hands-on.
s: Keep it up for ten minutes

actions.d: Warm water, calm music, no rush.
actions.w: Simple care for your body counts.

actions.t: Phone out of the bedroom tonight
actions.d: Charge it in another room and read or rest.
actions.w: Sleep fixes more than most apps can.
s: Charge your phone outside the bedroom

actions.d: A comforting drink or snack, just for you.
actions.w: Looking after yourself is a skill worth practising.
s: Eat or drink it at a table, no screen

actions.t: Write down what is worrying you
actions.d: Empty your head onto paper, then circle one thing you can act on.
actions.w: Worries shrink when they are written down.
s: Circle the one you can act on

actions.d: Alarm set, somewhere dark.
actions.w: Rest is productive.

actions.t: Visit a {newplace} you have never tried
actions.d: Somewhere nearby you always pass.
actions.w: New places make time feel fuller and more memorable.

actions.d: Get off a bus or metro somewhere new and wander.
actions.w: Adventure is closer than you think.

actions.d: Turn whichever way looks interesting.
actions.w: Serendipity without an algorithm.

actions.t: Find the oldest building near you
actions.d: Look for dates, old doors and faded signs.
actions.w: History in your own city gives perspective.
s: Read one fact about it later
